summary: Unexpected model-pin transfer after prewarm expiry causes silent fallback and duplicate billing
description:
Issue summary: Customer ClipperAI reports that during yesterday's staggered canary rollout their tenant traffic silently diverted to a degraded variant shortly after a prewarm step expired. Impact: multiple production requests returned the degraded model (gptx-3.0-quantized) for ~16 minutes and the customer observed a billing delta for both primary and degraded variant usage. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east-1, tenant-specific routing with model pin grace-period configured to 30s, prewarm window configured to 5m.

Observed behavior: At 2026-03-09T22:14:05Z the canary prewarm job finished and the tenant had an active pin to redwood-v2-medium. At 2026-03-09T22:19:12Z the pin lease expired but instead of keeping the tenant on the primary variant until explicit commit, control-plane initiated a silent transfer that left some edge nodes routing to gptx-3.0-quantized. This created mixed responses and duplicate tallying in usage metrics.

Expected behavior: Pin grace-period expiry should not trigger an automatic model transfer during a staggered prewarm unless orchestration confirms cohort commit. Tenant should either remain on primary variant or be explicitly failed over with audit log and customer-visible event.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Create staged canary with staggered prewarm (prewarm 5m, pin grace 30s). 2) Finish prewarm then intentionally delay canary commit by ~2 minutes. 3) Observe edge routing and billing metrics for cross-variant request counts and check control-plane commit logs.

Business impact: Customer reported degraded quality for conversation flows and unexpected billing spike across both variants; they are asking for a remediation timeline and potential credits.
steps_to_reproduce: Create dedicated tenant with staged canary and prewarm=5m, pin_grace=30s
Deploy redwood-v2-medium as primary and gptx-3.0-quantized as canary degraded variant
Allow prewarm to complete then delay commit signal for >60s
Generate steady traffic from tenant and observe routing traces and usage counters
logs: 2026-03-09T22:35:00Z control-plane: cohort_commit tenant=clipper-123 cohort=cohort-A commit_result=aborted reason=timeout
investigation_notes: Support triage: replicated customer traffic pattern in staging with identical prewarm/pin settings; observed local-edge cache divergence after lease expiry
Hypothesis 1: edge local routing cache fell back to last-seen prewarm mirror state when lease expired instead of honoring central locked pin until commit
Hypothesis 2: orchestrator's pin handoff path contains a race where a failed prewarm/commit leaves metadata in "transfer_pending" state; edge reconciler treats transfer_pending as a valid variant
Observed: some edges reported decision_source=local-cache while control-plane recorded lease_expired and then later abort commit
Billing team: usage records show near-equal token counts for both variants during 22:19–22:35 window; indicates synchronous duplicate accounting rather than sampling noise
comments: 2026-03-10T09:02Z - Luis Alvarez (Assignee): Thanks for the report, Maya. I've started a scoped repro in staging and linked the orchestrator PR that adjusted transfer semantics last month. Initial results show edge cache TTL interplay. (see related PR)
2026-03-10T10:18Z - Maya Chen (Support): Customer provided additional request ids and the Redbox traces. They want to know if traffic was doubled-charged or if it was misattributed across variants.

2026-03-10T13:45Z - Billing (Ana Rodriguez): Billing confirms two distinct usage records were emitted for the same client request batch. We're flagging those records for credit review; will coordinate once root cause is confirmed.

2026-03-11T08:30Z - SRE (Kai Patel): Found a code path where local-edge reconciliation treats transfer_pending as commit=true when lease expires mid-sync. Pushing a hotfix branch to gate the behavior behind a safety check.

2026-03-12T14:05Z - Luis Alvarez: Hotfix PR created and testing underway: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/4121. Mitigation for customers: extend pin_grace to 2m and disable staggered auto-commit until patch lands.
workaround: Recommended mitigation applied for ClipperAI: extended tenant pin_grace to 120s and temporarily disabled staggered auto-commit in the dedicated pool. These changes prevented further mixed-routing during the next prewarm window.
root_cause: Under investigation — initial SRE findings point to a race in the orchestrator's pin handoff logic where 'transfer_pending' metadata allowed edge reconcilers to consider the canary as active when central commit later aborted. Edge local-cache TTLs exacerbated the window of mixed routing.
resolution: In progress — hotfix PR to change transfer_pending semantics and add explicit 'force-hold-until-commit' flag for pin leases. Once validated, we'll coordinate a staged rollout and notify the customer. Billing has started credit assessment for the duplicated usage records.
postmortem_plan: If hotfix validates in staging, schedule emergency minor release to orchestrator, update runbook to recommend pin_grace >= prewarm window by default, add telemetry to detect duplicate-variant-usage spikes, and prepare customer-facing postmortem within 72 hours.
notes_for_engineering: Add a guard in edge reconciler to ignore transfer_pending until explicit commit or explicit failover
Ensure billing deduplication keys include commit id or lease id to avoid double-charge on transient mixed-routing
Instrument metric: duplicate_variant_usage_ratio per-tenant to surface future regressions
